summary: Implemented the AWS serverless deployment and human competition path for the Next.js research console. Added production and development SST/OpenNext stages, exact private asset buckets, CloudFront caching and invalidation, pinned Route 53/ACM domain wiring, and GitHub Actions OIDC deployments. Added a local-only deterministic competition game, GitHub Auth.js integration backed by AWS Secrets Manager, exact Lambda replay validation, a DynamoDB immutable-score ledger with a score GSI and dense 3-bit move storage, a versioned S3 game artifact, combined human/AI leaderboard filters, and replay pages. Repository-backed dynamic routes are staged into Lambda bundles without static export, and anonymous play performs no network submission.

The GitHub OAuth client fields in drop7-prod-github remain placeholders until the repository owner updates them manually; the generated AUTH_SECRET must be preserved.
GitHub OAuth Apps accept one callback URL, so development sign-in requires a second OAuth app and the optional development fields in the shared AWS secret.
The fixed competition future is public and reproducible, so human and AI scores are a scripted playground and never research-tier evidence.
The deployment exposes structured validation logs and operational metrics but does not collect passive browser analytics; any future analytics schema needs an explicit privacy and retention policy.
